digest.en: Russia's strike on a Ukrainian school killed twenty-six people, shattering fragile peace hopes. Simultaneously, Serbia's post-election chaos saw Vucic's crushing defeat trigger arrests and resignations. Moscow's military spending also gutted healthcare in poorer regions.
digest.hi: Houthi fighters launched coordinated strikes on Saudi Arabia, hitting Abha International Airport and Khmisa Air Base. The attacks come as Riyadh tightens security after a surge in regional tensions. Saudi officials say the raids were a warning to foreign forces stationed in the region.

articles.title: Clashes Near Kyiv Highlight Tension Over Military Manpower Challenges
articles.summary: Crowds clashed with Ukrainian riot police in a Kyiv suburb on November 2. The confrontation stemmed from military efforts to apprehend alleged deserters. Authorities are forcibly enlisting men to fight Russia. This incident highlights growing domestic tension over manpower shortages. Crowds clashed with Ukrainian riot police and national guardsmen in a Kyiv suburb on November 2 in the latest tensions over military efforts to catch alleged deserters and enlist men -- sometimes forcibly -- to fight in the war against Russia.

articles.title: Sanctions-evading China-bound billions turn untraceable in Moscow
articles.summary: Sanctions-evading funds destined for China become untraceable in Moscow. At the Sadovod market, eight distinct teams operate separately from regular vendors. These groups, called departments in confidential records, process a steady stream of customers. The setup obscures the financial trail of sanctioned goods. At the sprawling Sadovod market in southeast Moscow, among the 160 acres of clothing, jewelry and appliance booths, at least eight teams are spotted, working apart from the everyday hustle and bustle of the market.

articles.title: Russia's Poorer Regions Facing Brunt Of Health-Care Cuts As Military Spending Soars
articles.summary: Russia plans to cut funding for federal health-care programs in its 2027 budget. Medical services are already hard to access in many regions. The proposed reductions coincide with soaring military spending. Patients in poorer areas face greater obstacles to treatment and essential medicines. Russia plans to reduce funding for key federal health-care programs in its 2027 budget. With medical services already difficult to access in many regions, the proposed cuts are raising fears that patients will face greater obstacles in obtaining treatment and essential medicines.

articles.title: Trump’s troubles with Iran could open the door to China
articles.summary: China held a series of meetings with Gulf leaders to boost regional influence. This diplomatic push precedes a planned meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. articles.title: Air raid alerts and attacks on schools: the devastating face of education in Ukraine
articles.summary: UNICEF reported nearly 2,000 attacks on Ukrainian schools since 2022. Some 270 strikes occurred this year. A recent hit targeted a school distributing aid. The data highlights the severe impact on education infrastructure. Ukraine has sustained almost 2,000 attacks on education since the full-scale Russian invasion in 2022, with some 270 this year alone, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Tuesday, a day after a strike at a school being used to distribute aid.

articles.title: Ukrainian Crowd Clashes With Riot Police, Again Highlighting Recruitment Tactics, Military Morale
articles.summary: Residents clashed with police in a Kyiv suburb. Allegations of torture in a private house fueled the unrest. The incident underscores tensions over military recruitment tactics. Ukraine continues to manage domestic friction during the war. A crowd clashed with police and National Guard troops in a Kyiv suburb amid allegations that men were being held and tortured in a private house.

articles.title: Child dies of measles in New York's first such death in 30 years
articles.summary: A child died of measles in New York. It is the first such death in 30 years. Vaccination rates have dropped below the 95 percent threshold. This decline has allowed the virus to resurge in the United States. The U. S. stopped the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks of the viral disease.

articles.title: Strikes on a school by Russia kills 26, derailing hopes of progress toward peace
articles.summary: Russia resumed strikes on Kherson after a ceasefire ended. A school hit in the southern region killed 26 people. The attack derailed hopes for peace progress. Kyiv confirmed the resumption of hostilities in the area. Russia resumed its strikes on the southern region of Kherson after the end of a ceasefire in the area, the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours since Russia’s 2022 invasion, Kyiv said.

articles.title: Arrests, Resignations, Repainting: Here's What's Happening In Postelection Serbia
articles.summary: Serbia's political landscape shifted rapidly after Student List won the October 25 parliamentary elections. articles.title: After A Crushing Defeat, What Now For Serbia's Vucic?
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic stated he will return to power after his October election defeat. Legal challenges now threaten his political future. Prosecutors may pursue criminal charges against the former leader. His path back to office faces significant judicial hurdles. Former longstanding Serbian leader Aleksandar Vucic has said he’ll “come back” after losing elections in October. But is his future more likely to be in a court dock instead of the court of public opinion?

articles.title: Is Europe In Iran's Crosshairs? Tehran Hints At Wider Military Reach
articles.summary: Iran's supreme leader stated any future response to an attack would have no geographical limits. The remarks suggest Tehran may abandon its 2,000-kilometer missile range limit. Analysts speculate Europe could now fall within Iran's military reach. A statement attributed to Iran's supreme leader says any future response to an attack would have no geographical limits. The remarks have fueled speculation that Tehran could target Europe and abandon its self-imposed 2,000-kilometer limit on missile range.

articles.title: WFP provides hot meals to Oleshky evacuees as UN pushes to restore power before winter
articles.summary: The UN World Food Programme is feeding over 400 evacuees from Oleshky in Ukraine. These residents fled the Russian-occupied Kherson region during a brief local ceasefire. The agency is also working to restore power to the area before winter temperatures set in. The UN World Food Programme (WFP) is providing emergency food assistance to more than 400 people who were able to leave the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, during a brief local ceasefire.

articles.title: Six in seven journalist murders go unpunished, UNESCO reports
articles.summary: UNESCO reports that six in seven journalist murders go unpunished. Global impunity for these killings has risen for the first time in over a decade. The organization also flags the growing use of drones as an emerging threat to reporters working in active conflict zones. Global impunity for journalist killings has risen for the first time in more than a decade, while the growing use of drones is an emerging threat for reporters in conflict zones, according to the latest report from UN cultural organization UNESCO.

articles.title: Energy is America’s real weapon in a multipolar world
articles.summary: The United States is shifting its strategic focus from broad technological dominance to control over oil and gas. Washington now treats global energy supplies as its primary instrument of influence. Disrupting or threatening these finite commodities has become a central tool in a multipolar world. Faced with an emerging multipolar order, the United States appears to be relying less on dominance of every frontier technology than on leveraging its influence over the world’s most finite and strategically vital commodities: oil and gas.

articles.title: Trump’s Republicans brace for a midterm shellacking
articles.summary: US Republicans face a potentially punishing verdict in Tuesday's midterm elections. President Trump's approval rating stands at 32 percent in a recent poll. Democrats lead the national congressional ballot by more than eight percentage points, shifting the electoral map against the administration. WASHINGTON, D. C. US President Donald Trump’s Republicans enter Tuesday’s midterm elections facing a potentially punishing voter verdict. His approval rating stands at just 32% in a recent Reuters/Ipsos poll, while Democrats lead the national congressional ballot by more than eight percentage points.

articles.title: Victim's Family Speaks 2 Years After Serbia's Novi Sad Station Collapse
articles.summary: Andjela Ruman died in the Novi Sad station collapse in 2024. She was twenty when the canopy fell. Her parents, Zorica and Zlatko, discuss coping with the loss. Two years have passed since the incident. On November 1, 2024, 20-year-old Andjela Ruman arrived by train in Novi Sad, where her boyfriend was waiting for her. They died together when the station canopy collapsed.

articles.title: Breaking the silence in Mexico’s barracks
articles.summary: Investigative journalist Zorayda Gallegos documented sexual abuse within the Mexican armed forces. Many women in uniform reported that orders to enter an officer’s bedroom were treated as mandatory commands. The findings highlight a culture of unchecked authority and systemic harassment in the military ranks. In Mexico’s armed forces, an order from a superior is meant to be obeyed without question.

articles.title: UN ‘stands ready’ to keep supporting peace efforts as MINURSO mission ends
articles.summary: António Guterres stated the UN remains committed to a political solution in Western Sahara. The organization supports the self-determination of the local population. The UN remains committed to supporting a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution in Western Sahara that provides for the self-determination of its people, Secretary-General António Guterres said on Sunday, as the UN peacekeeping mission there began to wind down.

articles.summary: Giulia Paravicini reported from Asmara on life in Eritrea. She examined how the isolated nation's leadership calculates its position. articles.title: अर्नब और मुरासु के बाद कतार में कितने तूफान? क्या सर्दियों में ठंड बढ़ेगी या घटेगी
articles.summary: चक्रवात मुरासु आंध्र प्रदेश के तट पर कमजोर पड़ रहा है। इसके बाद भारी बारिश और पेड़ों के गिरने की खबरें आई हैं। यह एक सप्ताह में दूसरा तूफान है। पहले अर्नब का प्रकोप हुआ था। मौसम विभाग आगे के तूफानों की संभावना पर नजर रख रहा है। चक्रवात 'मुरासु' का असर अब कम होने लगा है. आंध्र प्रदेश के तट से टकराने के बाद यह कमजोर पड़ रहा है, लेकिन पीछे भारी बारिश, उखड़े पेड़ और बिजली के खंभों की तबाही छोड़ गया है.

articles.title: इजरायल में सत्ता की नई लड़ाई! लापिड ने नेतन्याहू को PMO से बाहर करने का उठाया मुद्दा
articles.summary: यायर लापिड ने बेंजामिन नेतन्याहू पर चुनाव परिणामों को कमजोर करने का आरोप लगाया। उन्होंने नेतन्याहू को पद से हटाने की मांग की। यह बयान राष्ट्रपति इसाक हर्ज़ोग से बातचीत से पहले आया। विपक्षी दलों के नेता हर्ज़लिया में एकत्र हुए। Israel Coalition Government: इजरायल के विपक्ष के नेता और ‘बीयाचाद’ (B’Yachad) पार्टी के दूसरे सबसे बड़े नेता यायर लापिड ने मंगलवार को प्रधानमंत्री बेंजामिन नेतन्याहू पर चुनाव परिणामों को कमजोर करने की कोशिश करने का आरोप लगाया और उन्हें पद से हटाने की मांग की।

articles.summary: बांग्लादेश में कपड़ा मजदूरों के हिंसक प्रदर्शनों के कारण भारत सतर्क है। विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता रणधीर जायसवाल ने कहा कि वे घटनाक्रम पर नजर बनाए हुए हैं। प्रदर्शनकारियों की मुख्य मांग वेतन में वृद्धि है। पड़ोसी बांग्लादेश में कपड़ा मजदूरों के उग्र विरोध-प्रदर्शन को लेकर भारत काफी सतर्कता बरत रहा है. भारतीय विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता रणधीर जायसवाल ने मंगलवार को नियमित प्रेस ब्रीफिंग के दौरान कहा कि बांग्लादेश के घटनाक्रमों को लेकर कहा कि वे लगातार नजर बनाए हुए हैं.

articles.title: लोगों ने हाथ लहराकर बुलाया और फिर...कैसे कटे 2 हेलीकॉप्टरों के धड़? सामने आए वीडियो ने सब साफ कर
articles.summary: नेपाल के माउंट एवरेस्ट क्षेत्र में फेरिचे पर दो हेलीकॉप्टरों के पंखे आपस में टकरा गए। वीडियो में जमीन पर खड़े लोगों ने पहले स्वागत किया, फिर भाग खड़े हुए। इस हादसे में फिशटेल एयर और एयर डायनेस्टी के विमान शामिल थे। नेपाल के माउंट एवरेस्ट इलाके में एक भयानक हेलीकॉप्टर हादसा हो गया. फेरिचे में लैंडिंग के वक्त फिशटेल एयर और एयर डायनेस्टी के दो हेलीकॉप्टरों के पंखे हवा में आपस में टकरा गए.

articles.title: ममता बनर्जी को सुप्रीम कोर्ट से बड़ा झटका, मीडिया ट्रायल पर रोक वाली याचिका खारिज
articles.summary: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने अभिषेक बनर्जी की याचिका खारिज कर दी। उन्होंने मीडिया रिपोर्टिंग पर रोक लगाने की मांग की थी। कोर्ट ने उन्हें दिवाली के बाद हाई कोर्ट में अंतरिम राहत के लिए जाने को कहा। सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने ममता बनर्जी की पार्टी के सांसद अभिषेक बनर्जी की याचिका खारिज कर दी, जिसमें उन्होंने अपने खिलाफ मामलों की मीडिया रिपोर्टिंग पर रोक लगाने की मांग की थी.
